title: Retrieval plane — candidate generation, fusion, reranking, and the diversity gap that wastes the context budget
description:
Third of seven plane epics (see `project-management/design/ADVANCED_MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md` and `project-management/AI_NATIVE_AGILE.md`).

**Invariant this plane owns:** every candidate carries a calibrated, comparable score.

**The objective function, stated once so every story below can be judged against it:** the target is not recall@k. It is *answer accuracy per token of assembled context*. Long context does not remove the need for memory — accuracy is a U-shaped function of position with >30% degradation for mid-context material (replicated across six model families), all 18 frontier models in the Chroma context-rot study degrade monotonically with input length even on trivially retrievable content, and LongMemEval measures a ~30% accuracy drop on sustained interactive memory in commercial assistants. A retrieval change that raises recall@20 while adding 3K tokens to the card is a regression under this objective, and stories here must report both numbers.

**A. Hybrid retrieval is currently vector plus a Python keyword-overlap ranker, and that under-performs on exactly the queries agent memory gets most.** The zero-infrastructure ranker was the right call for a dependency-light v1 and its RRF fusion (`repositories/base.py::_rrf_fuse`) is already correct — RRF is the right primitive precisely because it is score-scale invariant, so cosine distance and lexical scores never have to be made commensurable. What token-overlap cannot do is term weighting: proper nouns, identifiers, error codes, and rare tokens are exactly where dense retrieval is weakest and exactly where BM25's IDF term earns its keep. Whether Db2 gives us a usable text index for this, or whether it means a term-frequency side table, is not answerable from the docs and is spiked (RTRV-3).

**B. Contextual Retrieval is the highest measured ROI item in the entire v2 arc, and it drops into a table that already exists.** Prepending a short LLM-generated situating context to each chunk before embedding *and* before lexical indexing reports a 35% reduction in top-20 retrieval failure from contextual embeddings alone, 49% combined with contextual BM25, and 67% with reranking on top. `repositories/chunks.py` already stores chunk rows with overlapping 800-char windows; this is a `context_prefix` column and a change to what gets embedded. The cost is an LLM call per chunk at index time, amortised by prompt caching to roughly $1 per million document tokens — and it is a *write-path* cost, so it does not touch read latency at all.

**C. Nothing in the pipeline penalises redundancy, and agent memory is pathologically redundant.** The same preference restated across twelve sessions produces twelve high-scoring near-duplicates, and top-k by score returns k paraphrases of one thing while the budget that could have carried k distinct facts is spent. MMR is a ~40-line greedy pass over the fused candidate list with one tunable, and under the accuracy-per-token objective it is among the cheapest real wins available.

**D. Weights are guessed, and the code does not currently emit what it would take to stop guessing.** `benchmarks/scoring_weights.yaml` exists and is the right home for a fitted scoring function, but `search()` returns a fused ordering without the per-component contributions (relevance, recency, importance, confidence, frequency, decay) that produced it. Logging those alongside each result is unglamorous and is the prerequisite for RTRV-4 and for every weight decision in EPIC-31.

**E. Two-stage retrieval is nearly free and we are not doing it.** Matryoshka-trained embeddings nest coarse information in their leading dimensions, so a shortlist can be generated on 64-256 dims and reranked exactly on the full width. Cross-encoder reranking is the quality ceiling above that, but it is a per-candidate forward pass and whether the latency budget tolerates it is a real question, not a given (RTRV-8). The Matryoshka half is filed under EPIC-28 (VIDX-8) because it is primarily an index storage change; the reranking half is here.

**Deliberately out of scope:** ColBERT-style late interaction. It is the known quality ceiling and PLAID makes it tractable, but one vector per token is a storage cost this SDK should not take on speculatively. It stays a documented ceiling until an ablation demands it.

**Depends on:** EPIC-28 VIDX-3 for a recall baseline before any latency-affecting change. RTRV-1 touches `chunks.py`, which EPIC-28 VIDX-5 also touches — sequence them or expect a conflict.
**Blocks:** EPIC-33 (assembly has nothing to pack without calibrated scores).
